rationale.complete: Round 1 done: synthetic validation (rerun with the amended estimator), dated predictions, 13 per-period folders plus NE10 and the undocumented 08-20 nudger stop, scorecard, confirmatory script written and dry-run. Holdout not run; only one powered (short-pause) period. Round 1b: glance, sustained-run and work-commit outcomes, efficiencies and policy per outcome, natives NE10/NE43 on the work ledger and G38 vs G51.
rationale.faithfulness: In G51 the demon bookkeeping beats its nulls. Information is above the permutation null, the response is heterogeneous (R0 rejected) and the efficiency is well below 1 (R1 rejected). The predicted information magnitude and agent-blindness failed, and P4 failed as worded (negative value of information among gates, a stronger inefficiency). The response pattern reverses in the long-pause periods. Scorecard A1 B1 C1 D1 E1 F1 G1 H1 I1; no holdout.
rationale.usefulness: The once-early policy still triples active minutes per nudge, but on the work ledger nudges buy no commits or sustained runs, so the lever moves attention, not output (usefulness 2.5 -> 2.0).

one_line: The nudger is an inefficient Maxwell demon for activity (38% efficiency; nudge once, early) and a worthless one for work: it buys glances, not commits.

models.note: demon accounting holds for activity; zero value for committed work
gate model: response falls with trap age for minutes only

raters.claim: Scope: G51 (only powered period). A first auto-nudge buys a small activity response (+1.45 active min, glance +0.08, placebo clean) at well below its information frontier (eta_SU ~0.38; once-early nudging x2.3 active minutes), and no detectable committed work.
